extracted.intended_audience: professional photojournalists and documentary photographers (potential entrants)
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting photojournalism or documentary photography to the 2026 World Press Photo Contest, following eligibility, technical, captioning, category and judging rules. Includes registering on Picter, proving professional status, and meeting deadlines and manipulation/verification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / Professional status
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is free and open to professional photojournalists and documentary photographers. Registration requires personal data and proof of professional status; new entrants (those who have not entered in the last three years) will have their registration reviewed to ensure it meets entry rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While registration is under review you may upload work. World Press Photo reserves the right to request additional information to clarify professional status. See full entry rules for specific eligibility definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production timeframe / Period of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest recognizes the best photojournalism and documentary photography produced over the last year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries for the 2026 contest are accepted from 1 December 2025, 13.00 CET until 17 January 2026, 13.00 CET. Entrants must ensure their work falls within the contest's allowed production period as stated in the entry rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual quality — can include creativity, technical skill and visual style, and the edit of the story (where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jury is asked to consider visual creativity and technical execution when judging images or stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story (relevance and approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Story — refers to the story and/or issues covered in the photographs, its relevance or significance, and the way in which the photographer has chosen to approach the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges assess the subject matter's importance and the photographer's editorial/visual approach to conveying the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation / diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation — the importance of awarding a diverse range of stories and photographers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo encourages a multiplicity of stories and diverse photographers; the jury should consider representation among entries and winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and regional allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be entered into the contest categories and regions; winners are allocated across categories and regions (42 contest winners: three Singles, three Stories and one Long-Term Project per region — regions listed include Africa; Asia-Pacific and Oceania; Europe; North and Central America; South America; West, Central, and South Asia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must consult the contest categories and regions pages to choose the correct category/region. The regional/category structure affects allocation of awards and eligibility for certain prizes (e.g., Photo of the Year selection is from the 42 winners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions and metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must add captions, metadata and other information for their uploaded work and follow the contest's guidance on how to write captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'what is required in captions' guidance page for instructions; accurate captions and metadata are part of the submission requirements and will be used in judging and exhibition/publication contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must meet the contest's technical requirements (file formats, sizes, resolution and other technical specifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the contest technical requirements page for exact specifications. Failure to meet technical specs may render an entry ineligible or unshowable in exhibitions/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification process and manipulation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a verification process including manipulation rules that govern permissible edits and image integrity for submitted photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must comply with verification and manipulation rules; the contest may verify authenticity and disqualify or penalize entries that breach manipulation or ethical standards. See the verification-process page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and jury discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Although World Press Photo provides criteria to guide the jury, the jury is independent and has the freedom to determine and define what makes an entry worthy of an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization asks jurors to consider specified criteria (visual quality, story, representation) but does not restrict jurors from applying their professional judgment; jurors come from diverse regional and industry backgrounds and bring different insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter, create a Picter account, register for the 2026 World Press Photo Contest (providing required personal data and proof), upload work, add required captions/metadata, and submit entries before the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While registration may be under review, uploading is allowed; final submission must occur before 17 January 2026, 13.00 CET. Follow the 'how to enter' instructions and ensure all required fields and proofs are provided.
